title: The Tree of Life
events_chronological: Mrs O'Brien is taught by nuns that there are two ways through life, the way of nature and the way of grace.
Mr and Mrs O'Brien marry and their first son Jack is born.
Two more sons follow, and the three boys run wild through the summers of a small Texas town.
Mr O'Brien drills the boys in discipline at the dinner table and teaches the middle one the guitar.
Mrs O'Brien plays with the boys on the lawn while their father is away on business.
Jack, jealous and confused, breaks a neighbour's window and steals a slip from a woman's drawer.
Jack takes his brother into the yard and persuades him to put a finger over an air rifle, then shoots him.
Mr O'Brien loses his job when the plant closes and the family have to leave the house.
Jack asks his brother's forgiveness in a doorway without being able to say any of the words.
A telegram arrives to say the middle brother has died at nineteen, and Mrs O'Brien cannot be consoled.
Mr O'Brien tells Jack that he was too hard on all of them.
The universe forms, stars collapse, the earth cools, and the first life appears in the sea.
A wounded creature lies in a river bed while another puts a foot on its head and then lets it live.
Jack, a middle-aged architect in a glass tower, cannot get through the anniversary of his brother's death.
Jack walks through a doorway standing alone in a desert and finds everyone he has lost gathered on a shore.
syuzhet_notes: The film is cut to whispered prayer rather than to sequence, and the twenty-minute passage on the formation of the universe interrupts the family story without belonging anywhere in it. Nothing announces which period a shot is in.
fabula_notes: The chronology of the family material is fixed by the boys' ages. The cosmological passage and the closing shore are placed here at the points the film's own logic implies, but neither is dated.
